concept.name: Initiative buying
concept.definition: In Market Profile/auction terminology, initiative buying is aggressive buying occurring at or above the established value area — activity that is 'unexpected' at those prices because buyers are paying up through accepted value to push the auction toward new, higher value. It is the buying side of other-timeframe participation that breaks balance and drives range extension.
concept.intuition: Responsive buyers wait for cheap prices; initiative buyers chase — they buy where value already is, or above it, because they want prices to go higher.
concept.mechanics: Identified by location relative to the prior value area (buying at/above VAH) combined with conviction evidence: range extension beyond the initial balance, one-time-framing, and — on footprints — stacked buy imbalances and positive delta.
concept.failure_modes: The initiative/responsive classification depends entirely on where value is drawn, so mis-measured value areas mislabel the activity; initiative buying can also be immediately absorbed and fail (a failed auction).
concept.misconceptions: Initiative buying is not inherently 'smart money' to copy — late initiative buyers are routinely trapped at extremes, which is exactly what poor highs and failed auctions record.
concept.example: Price opens above yesterday's VAH and buyers keep lifting offers through the first hour, extending the range with stacked buy imbalances; the activity is read as initiative buying, favoring trend-following tactics over fading.

citations.source: FuturesIndicators — Trading With Market Profile: Practical Setups (responsive vs initiative activity)
